page: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 64-bit ARM architecture running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile supplies 32 dedicated vCPUs paired with 256 GB of system memory, yielding an 8 GB memory-to-core ratio. The server does not incorporate graphics processing units or hardware accelerators.

Local ephemeral storage is provided via 1888 GB of integrated NVMe SSD space, enabling high-throughput data processing for temporary volumes, paging, and scratch operations. In addition to local storage, the instance supports Azure Premium Storage for attached persistent disk volumes. Networking provisions include no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating virtual network configuration or private endpoint routing for external network egress.

The ARM processor architecture delivers high compute and memory density, providing strong operational cost efficiency for systems scaling across significant memory footprints. A architectural tradeoff is the absence of x86 vector extensions, requiring binaries to be compiled specifically for arm64. Given the balanced 1:8 compute-to-memory profile and bundled NVMe scratch disk, the instance is structured for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, relational database engines, and memory-constrained analytical workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v7 is an arm64 memory-optimized virtual machine providing 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. Operated under Microsoft Hyper-V, the platform bundles 1888 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Azure Premium Storage for persistent workloads. The configuration excludes GPUs and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The ARM-based architecture provides efficient resource scaling and high memory density relative to standard compute classes, though software must support arm64 execution environments. With extensive memory capacity and fast local NVMe temporary storage, this instance is suited for in-memory caching solutions, large relational database backends, and high-throughput data processing tasks requiring substantial working memory.
